headline: Southborough advanced a $38 million Neary School addition-renovation plan, decided Special Town Meeting articles, and initiated FY28 budget and capital planning.
synopsis: During October, Southborough boards addressed major decisions concerning school facilities, Town Meeting warrant articles, and upcoming fiscal planning. The Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance a $38 million addition-renovation design for Neary Elementary School after analyses determined a smaller $15 million scope could not satisfy building codes or facility needs. At the October Special Town Meeting, voters approved Community Preservation Act funding for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge, while a proposed two-family zoning amendment fell short of a two-thirds majority. Departments across town began building fiscal year 2028 operating and capital budgets, preparing dual tracks to account for potential override constraints. Meanwhile, the Personnel Board adopted a 60th percentile salary benchmark for municipal employees, and environmental reviews opened for the proposed Costco development.

top_items.title: Neary School addition-renovation advances to schematic design
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted 4-0 to advance Option 3 to schematic design after architects found a $15 million renovation would fund only $5.8 million in direct repairs.
top_items.body: Architectural analysis revealed that building-code triggers for full fire sprinkler and accessibility upgrades would consume most of a $15 million budget, leaving major boiler and univent replacements unfunded. The committee voted unanimously to authorize Tappé Architects to develop schematic design drawings and detailed cost models for the $38 million addition-renovation option. Municipal and school officials will evaluate whether to seek Massachusetts School Building Authority reimbursement or fund the project locally.

top_items.title: Special Town Meeting rejects two-family zoning amendment
top_items.why: A proposed zoning amendment to ease conversions of two-family dwellings failed to achieve the necessary two-thirds majority at Special Town Meeting, despite an 85-80 vote in favor.
top_items.body: The article had received support from the Select Board, Planning Board, and Affordable Housing Trust, but faced skepticism regarding density and minimum lot size requirements. Following the defeat, the Zoning Board of Appeals agreed to pause further local bylaw amendments and monitor pending state legislation regarding two-family housing. The Affordable Housing Trust noted the vote underscored the ongoing need for public education on housing diversity.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail footbridge secures Town Meeting funding
top_items.why: Special Town Meeting approved $217,318 in Community Preservation Act funding for the Peninsula Trail Phase 2 footbridge following a 3-2 CPC vote to advance the article.
top_items.body: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send the funding request to town meeting as written, declining to eliminate project contingencies through floor amendments. Voters subsequently passed the appropriation, bringing total authorized funding to $428,550 despite negative recommendations from the Select Board and Advisory Committee. The Trails Committee is now assembling a MassTrails grant application for up to $100,000 to offset municipal costs and is coordinating pedestrian crossings on Route 30 and Central Street.

top_items.title: Personnel Board adopts 60th percentile compensation benchmark
top_items.why: The Personnel Board voted unanimously to set the 60th percentile of regional comparable towns as the salary benchmark for its municipal compensation study.
top_items.body: The compensation study presented by MGT recommended replacing the current 9-grade system with a 12-grade structure covering non-union municipal staff. In response to feedback from department heads regarding job grading and titles, the board established a three-member panel to handle appeals and set a submission deadline of November 24, 2026. The new classification and compensation plan is slated for consideration at the Annual Town Meeting to take effect July 1, 2027.

top_items.title: Capital committee reviews $2.15M requests and major bonding
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began reviewing FY28 requests totaling $2.152 million in appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable projects.
top_items.body: The capital submissions include $710,000 in local school requests for sink replacements, stair repairs, and drainage fencing, as well as Department of Public Works vehicle replacements and facilities work. Committee members evaluated whether to recommend lowering the town bonding threshold from $300,000 to $200,000 to shift large items into borrowing articles. The committee scheduled joint sessions with the Select Board and Advisory Committee to align on the town's debt capacity.

top_items.title: Costco warehouse enters conservation and stormwater reviews
top_items.why: The Conservation Commission opened its public hearing on the Notice of Intent and stormwater permit for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco on Coslin Drive.
top_items.body: The applicant presented environmental plans for the 22-acre site featuring a 30-position gas station, deep-sump catch basins, hydrodynamic separators, and two constructed stormwater wetland basins. Meanwhile, the Planning Board extended its decision deadline to December 18 to complete regional traffic reviews, and the town administrator confirmed special state legislation was enacted authorizing an off-premises alcohol license for the store.

top_items.title: School Committee amends teachers contract and aligns salaries
top_items.why: The Southborough School Committee voted 5-0 to approve contract amendments with the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A.
top_items.body: The amendments adjust the retirement incentive program and align the Southborough elementary and middle school teacher salary schedule with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027. The committee also noted that the Neary Elementary School roof replacement is nearing completion roughly $1.6 million under its $4.5 million borrowing authorization, and approved its FY28 operating budget guidelines.
